question: How Do I See Subscription Revenue Reports in WooCommerce?
metaDescription: WooCommerce Subscriptions adds its own reports for renewal revenue, signups and retention — here's where to find them and what each one actually shows.
shortAnswer: WooCommerce Subscriptions adds dedicated reports under WooCommerce → Analytics (or the older Reports screen, depending on version), covering signups, renewals, and retention over a chosen date range — separate from the regular order/revenue reports, which don't distinguish a subscription renewal from a one-time sale.

bodyHtml:
Where to Find Them

Look under WooCommerce → Analytics → Subscriptions (or Reports → Subscriptions on older setups). The dedicated reports break out signups, renewals, and cancellations as distinct events, and calculate recurring-revenue figures specifically — something the regular WooCommerce order reports don't do, since to them a renewal order just looks like any other completed order.

What Each Report Actually Shows

  • Signups — new subscriptions started in the selected period, useful for tracking acquisition trends separate from renewal revenue.
  • Renewals — recurring revenue collected in the period, distinguishing it from one-time purchase revenue mixed into it.
  • Cancellations and switches — useful for tracking churn and understanding whether customers are downgrading, upgrading, or leaving entirely.
  • Retention/renewal rate — the proportion of subscriptions that successfully renew versus those that fail or get cancelled, a core health metric for a subscription business.

Getting More Out of It

  1. Use these reports instead of the regular order reports when the question is specifically about subscription health — mixing renewal revenue into general sales figures makes trends harder to read accurately.
  2. Export the underlying data if a metric not directly shown (like revenue per specific product tier) needs its own custom breakdown, since the built-in reports cover the common cases but not every possible cut of the data.
  3. For metrics beyond what's built in — cohort retention curves, lifetime value by acquisition channel, and similar — that typically needs either a dedicated analytics plugin or a custom reporting build against the REST API or database.

See custom WooCommerce development for subscription analytics beyond what the built-in reports cover.
